steps.thought: I will list the available tests to see what diagnostic options are available for the drone assembly line.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly check all communication buses and device enumeration before deciding on more expensive subsystem tests.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed successfully with all expected I2C, UART, and CAN devices enumerated correctly and a boot time of 1898 ms.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power on self test passed cleanly with no detected failures across subsystems, though further testing is required.
Basic power-on passed, but motor mechanical issues would not manifest until motor spin tests are run.
ESC issues might not appear during a static low-power selftest until telemetry and spin tests are conducted.
Resting voltage and cell degradation require dedicated battery testing to rule out completely.
Device enumeration succeeded, but IMU calibration and noise profiles require static IMU testing.

steps.thought: I will run the battery_rest_check to verify cell balance and resting voltage as a quick and inexpensive next step to cover the battery subsystem.
steps.observation: The battery_rest_check passed with normal pack voltage and low cell imbalance, ruling out immediate battery cell failure.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on selftest and resting battery check both passed with no anomalous readings across checked subsystems.
Mechanical motor wear will not be visible until motor spin or telemetry tests are executed.
ESC communication or commutation issues require dedicated telemetry or motor tests to detect.
IMU enumeration succeeded, but calibration and noise parameters require dedicated IMU testing.
Camera enumerated over UART, but CSI signal integrity or ribbon faults require camera selftest to confirm.

steps.thought: Run esc_telemetry to check commutation sync and telemetry status, as it is a low-cost test that covers the ESC subsystem.
steps.observation: The esc_telemetry test failed with 27 sync errors on esc_3, indicating a commutation or timing issue on motor/ESC position 3. All other ESCs passed with minimal sync errors.

hypotheses.rationale: High sync error count specifically on esc_3 points directly to an ESC commutation desync or firmware timing issue on that channel.
Mechanical drag from a degraded bearing could potentially contribute to ESC sync errors, though motor tests are needed to confirm.
An intermittent winding short could cause commutation difficulties, but further motor testing is required.

steps.thought: Run motor_spin_test to check the RPM jitter, current draw, and temperature on esc_3 / motor_3 to confirm whether the sync errors are caused by an ESC commutation desync or a motor winding/bearing issue.
steps.observation: The motor_spin_test revealed severe abnormalities on motor_3, including low RPM (3660) and extreme RPM jitter (1180), which strongly corroborate the high sync errors previously found on esc_3.

hypotheses.rationale: High sync errors on esc_3 combined with massive RPM jitter and low RPM on motor_3 suggest a commutation or ESC synchronization failure.
Severe mechanical drag or binding in the bearing of motor_3 could explain the high current draw, low RPM, and resulting sync failures.
An inter-turn winding short on motor_3 could also cause reduced RPM and commutation sync issues.

steps.thought: The unit exhibits high sync errors on esc_3 (27 errors) and extremely low RPM with massive RPM jitter on motor_3 during the spin test. This points to a commutation/synchronization failure of ESC 3.
